questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: A global enterprise has multiple AWS Regions and needs a centralized way to manage their global network, segment traffic between 'production' and 'development' environments globally, and automate the attachment of new VPCs across all regions. The solution should minimize operational overhead and provide a unified dashboard for network visibility.

options.text: Use AWS Cloud WAN to create a global core network. Define segments for production and development, and use attachment policies to automatically map new VPCs to the correct segment based on resource tags.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Cloud WAN provides a managed global wide area network (WAN) that allows you to build, manage, and monitor a unified global network. It supports network segmentation and automated attachments based on tags, significantly reducing operational overhead compared to manual routing.

options.text: Use AWS Transit Gateway with inter-region peering. Create separate route tables for production and development, and write AWS Lambda functions to detect new VPCs and update route tables automatically across all regions.
options.explanation: Incorrect: While Transit Gateway supports inter-region peering and segmentation via route tables, managing this globally requires significant manual configuration or custom automation (like Lambda), which introduces higher operational overhead and lacks a unified global management dashboard.

options.text: Use AWS Direct Connect Gateway to connect all VPCs across all regions. Segment the traffic using Security Groups and Network ACLs in every individual VPC, managing rules centrally using AWS Firewall Manager.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Direct Connect Gateway is primarily designed to connect on-premises networks to AWS VPCs, not for inter-region VPC-to-VPC routing. Furthermore, relying solely on Security Groups for global segmentation is difficult to manage at scale.

options.text: Use VPC Peering to establish a full mesh of peering connections across all regions. Manage route tables in each VPC to segment production and development traffic, using automation scripts to handle updates.
options.explanation: Incorrect: VPC Peering does not scale well for global networks due to the full mesh requirement, which limits the number of connections and drastically increases the operational overhead of managing complex routing tables manually.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Cloud WAN provides a centralized dashboard to build, manage, and monitor a unified global network. It uses attachment policies and network segments to automate the routing of traffic across multiple regions, natively satisfying the requirement to isolate production and development traffic while minimizing operational overhead.

pt.domainName: Domínio 1: Design de Soluções para Complexidade Organizacional
pt.statement: Uma empresa global possui múltiplas regiões da AWS e precisa de uma maneira centralizada para gerenciar sua rede global, segmentar o tráfego entre ambientes de 'produção' e 'desenvolvimento' globalmente, e automatizar a anexação de novas VPCs em todas as regiões. A solução deve minimizar a sobrecarga operacional e fornecer um painel unificado para visibilidade da rede.

options.text: Usar o AWS Cloud WAN para criar uma rede central global. Definir segmentos para produção e desenvolvimento, e usar políticas de anexação para mapear automaticamente novas VPCs para o segmento correto com base em tags de recursos.
options.explanation: Correto: O AWS Cloud WAN fornece uma rede de longa distância (WAN) global gerenciada que permite construir, gerenciar e monitorar uma rede global unificada. Ele suporta segmentação de rede e anexações automatizadas baseadas em tags, reduzindo significativamente a sobrecarga operacional em comparação com o roteamento manual.

options.text: Usar o AWS Transit Gateway com peering entre regiões. Criar tabelas de rotas separadas para produção e desenvolvimento, e escrever funções AWS Lambda para detectar novas VPCs e atualizar as tabelas de rotas automaticamente em todas as regiões.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Embora o Transit Gateway suporte peering entre regiões e segmentação via tabelas de rotas, gerenciar isso globalmente requer configuração manual significativa ou automação personalizada (como Lambda), o que introduz maior sobrecarga operacional e carece de um painel de gerenciamento global unificado.

options.text: Usar o AWS Direct Connect Gateway para conectar todas as VPCs em todas as regiões. Segmentar o tráfego usando Security Groups e Network ACLs em cada VPC individualmente, gerenciando as regras centralmente usando o AWS Firewall Manager.
options.explanation: Incorreto: O AWS Direct Connect Gateway foi projetado principalmente para conectar redes locais a VPCs da AWS, não para roteamento inter-regiões entre VPCs. Além disso, depender exclusivamente de Security Groups para segmentação global é difícil de gerenciar em grande escala.

options.text: Usar VPC Peering para estabelecer uma malha completa de conexões de peering em todas as regiões. Gerenciar as tabelas de rotas em cada VPC para segmentar o tráfego de produção e desenvolvimento, usando scripts de automação para lidar com atualizações.
options.explanation: Incorreto: O VPC Peering não escala bem para redes globais devido ao requisito de malha completa, o que limita o número de conexões e aumenta drasticamente a sobrecarga operacional de gerenciar tabelas de roteamento complexas manualmente.

pt.generalExplanation: O AWS Cloud WAN fornece um painel centralizado para construir, gerenciar e monitorar uma rede global unificada. Ele usa políticas de anexação e segmentos de rede para automatizar o roteamento de tráfego em múltiplas regiões, satisfazendo nativamente o requisito de isolar o tráfego de produção e desenvolvimento enquanto minimiza a sobrecarga operacional.

questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: A company is migrating its microservices to AWS, running on Amazon EC2, Amazon EKS, and AWS Lambda across multiple VPCs and AWS accounts. They need a consistent way to discover, connect, and secure communication between these services with fine-grained identity-based access control, without managing complex network routing or configuring API Gateways for internal traffic.

options.text: Deploy a centralized AWS Transit Gateway to connect all VPCs. Use Security Groups and Network ACLs to control traffic. Deploy an internal Application Load Balancer in front of each service and configure cross-account access.
options.explanation: Incorrect: This approach requires managing complex network routing, overlapping IP addresses, and configuring separate load balancers for each service. It also relies on network-level controls rather than the fine-grained, identity-based access control requested for the microservices.

options.text: Implement AWS PrivateLink for all services. Create a VPC Endpoint Service for each microservice in the provider accounts and Interface VPC Endpoints in consuming VPCs. Use VPC Endpoint Policies for fine-grained access control.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Creating and managing VPC Endpoint Services and Interface Endpoints for hundreds of microservices across multiple accounts introduces significant operational overhead and complexity, making it difficult to maintain consistent identity-based access control at scale compared to VPC Lattice.

options.text: Use AWS App Mesh by deploying Envoy proxies as sidecars for all EC2 and EKS workloads. Create an internal Amazon API Gateway to handle routing to Lambda functions and integrate with AWS Identity and Access Management.
options.explanation: Incorrect: While AWS App Mesh provides service mesh capabilities, it requires managing Envoy proxies and doesn't natively simplify cross-VPC and cross-account network routing as easily as VPC Lattice. Additionally, using API Gateway for internal Lambda routing adds unnecessary complexity.

options.text: Use Amazon VPC Lattice to create a service network spanning the different accounts and VPCs. Define services for the EC2, EKS, and Lambda workloads and use auth policies to enforce fine-grained, identity-based access control.
options.explanation: Correct: Amazon VPC Lattice is an application networking service that simplifies connecting, securing, and monitoring services across VPCs and accounts. It handles service discovery and allows implementing identity-based authentication and authorization policies without complex network routing.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon VPC Lattice provides a fully managed application networking capability that allows you to easily connect, secure, and monitor communications between services spanning multiple AWS accounts and VPCs. It abstracts away the complexity of routing, IP overlap, and load balancing, while natively supporting identity-based access control via auth policies.

pt.statement: Uma empresa está migrando seus microsserviços para a AWS, executando no Amazon EC2, Amazon EKS e AWS Lambda em múltiplas VPCs e contas AWS. options.text: Implantar um AWS Transit Gateway centralizado para conectar todas as VPCs. Usar Security Groups e Network ACLs para controlar o tráfego. Implantar um Application Load Balancer interno na frente de cada serviço e configurar acesso entre contas.

options.text: Implementar AWS PrivateLink para todos os serviços. Criar um VPC Endpoint Service para cada microsserviço nas contas provedoras e Interface VPC Endpoints nas VPCs consumidoras. Usar Políticas de Endpoint VPC para controle de acesso refinado.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Criar e gerenciar Serviços de Endpoint VPC e Endpoints de Interface para centenas de microsserviços em várias contas introduz complexidade e sobrecarga operacional significativas, dificultando a manutenção do controle de acesso baseado em identidade de forma consistente em escala, em comparação com o VPC Lattice.

Além disso, usar o API Gateway para roteamento interno de Lambda adiciona complexidade desnecessária.

options.text: Usar o Amazon VPC Lattice para criar uma rede de serviços abrangendo as diferentes contas e VPCs. Definir serviços para as cargas de trabalho do EC2, EKS e Lambda e usar políticas de autenticação para impor controle de acesso refinado baseado em identidade.
options.explanation: Correto: O Amazon VPC Lattice é um serviço de rede de aplicações que simplifica a conexão, segurança e monitoramento de serviços em VPCs e contas. questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: A financial organization must enforce strict security controls by blocking outbound DNS queries from their Amazon VPCs to known malicious domains. They also need to allowlist specific domains required for internal applications to function properly, while logging all DNS query attempts for compliance auditing.

options.text: Configure VPC Network ACLs to block port 53 traffic to specific IP addresses associated with malicious domains. Allow traffic only to the IP addresses of the internal application domains and enable VPC Flow Logs.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Network ACLs operate at the IP address layer, not the DNS layer. Blocking IP addresses does not prevent DNS queries from being resolved by the Amazon-provided DNS server, and managing a list of malicious IPs is highly inefficient.

options.text: Use AWS WAF by associating a Web ACL with the Route 53 public hosted zone. Create rules to block requests matching the malicious domain patterns and allow the internal application domains, logging requests to Amazon S3.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS WAF is designed to protect web applications running on resources like Application Load Balancers, API Gateway, or CloudFront from web exploits. It cannot be used to filter outbound DNS queries originating from resources within an Amazon VPC.

options.text: Deploy AWS Network Firewall in a centralized inspection VPC using AWS Transit Gateway. Configure stateful rules to inspect DNS traffic and drop packets destined for malicious domains based on Server Name Indication (SNI) headers.
options.explanation: Incorrect: While AWS Network Firewall can inspect and filter traffic, routing all DNS queries through a centralized inspection VPC for filtering adds unnecessary latency and complexity compared to using the natively integrated Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall.

options.text: Implement Amazon Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall. Create rule groups with a block list for malicious domains and an allow list for specific internal domains. Associate the rule groups with the VPCs and enable query logging.
options.explanation: Correct: Amazon Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall allows you to filter and regulate outbound DNS traffic for your VPCs. You can easily create block and allow lists for specific domains and log all DNS queries to Amazon CloudWatch for auditing purposes.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall is the purpose-built service for filtering outbound DNS queries originating from within a VPC. It allows administrators to define domain lists (blocklists and allowlists) to prevent DNS resolution of known malicious domains while permitting necessary internal traffic. Furthermore, it natively integrates with Route 53 query logging to provide complete audit trails.

pt.domainName: Domínio 1: Design de Soluções para Complexidade Organizacional
pt.statement: Uma organização financeira deve impor controles de segurança rigorosos, bloqueando consultas DNS de saída de suas VPCs da Amazon para domínios maliciosos conhecidos. Eles também precisam adicionar à lista de permissões domínios específicos exigidos para que os aplicativos internos funcionem corretamente, enquanto registram todas as tentativas de consulta DNS para auditoria de conformidade.

options.text: Configurar Network ACLs de VPC para bloquear o tráfego da porta 53 para endereços IP específicos associados a domínios maliciosos. Permitir tráfego apenas para os endereços IP dos domínios do aplicativo interno e habilitar os VPC Flow Logs.
options.explanation: Incorreto: As Network ACLs operam na camada de endereço IP, não na camada DNS. Bloquear endereços IP não impede que as consultas DNS sejam resolvidas pelo servidor DNS fornecido pela Amazon, e gerenciar uma lista de IPs maliciosos é altamente ineficiente.

options.text: Usar o AWS WAF associando uma Web ACL à zona hospedada pública do Route 53. Criar regras para bloquear solicitações que correspondam aos padrões de domínio malicioso e permitir os domínios do aplicativo interno, registrando solicitações no Amazon S3.
options.explanation: Incorreto: O AWS WAF foi projetado para proteger aplicativos web executados em recursos como Application Load Balancers, API Gateway ou CloudFront contra vulnerabilidades web. Ele não pode ser usado para filtrar consultas DNS de saída originadas de recursos dentro de uma Amazon VPC.

options.text: Implantar o AWS Network Firewall em uma VPC de inspeção centralizada usando o AWS Transit Gateway. Configurar regras com estado para inspecionar o tráfego DNS e descartar pacotes destinados a domínios maliciosos com base em cabeçalhos Server Name Indication (SNI).
options.explanation: Incorreto: Embora o AWS Network Firewall possa inspecionar e filtrar o tráfego, rotear todas as consultas DNS por meio de uma VPC de inspeção centralizada para filtragem adiciona latência e complexidade desnecessárias em comparação com o uso do Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall integrado de forma nativa.

options.text: Implementar o Amazon Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall. Criar grupos de regras com uma lista de bloqueio para domínios maliciosos e uma lista de permissões para domínios internos específicos. Associar os grupos de regras às VPCs e habilitar o log de consultas.
options.explanation: Correto: O Amazon Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall permite filtrar e regular o tráfego DNS de saída para suas VPCs. Você pode criar facilmente listas de bloqueio e permissão para domínios específicos e registrar todas as consultas DNS no Amazon CloudWatch para fins de auditoria.

options.text: Configurar Network ACLs de VPC para bloquear el tráfico del puerto 53 a direcciones IP específicas asociadas con dominios maliciosos. Permitir el tráfico solo a las direcciones IP de los dominios de la aplicación interna y habilitar VPC Flow Logs.

options.explanation: Incorrecto: AWS WAF está diseñado para proteger aplicaciones web que se ejecutan en recursos como Application Load Balancers, API Gateway o CloudFront de vulnerabilidades web. es.generalExplanation: Amazon Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall es el servicio diseñado específicamente para filtrar las consultas DNS salientes que se originan dentro de una VPC. Además, se integra de forma nativa con el registro de consultas de Route 53 para proporcionar pistas de auditoría completas.

questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: A software company operates hundreds of microservices using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). They require a dynamic service discovery mechanism that allows services to discover each other. Crucially, some services must discover endpoints by querying custom operational attributes instead of relying solely on standard IP addresses and port numbers.

options.text: Use Amazon Route 53 private hosted zones and configure the Amazon ECS services to register their IP addresses as A records. Use standard DNS queries to discover services based on custom attributes embedded in the TXT records.
options.explanation: Incorrect: DNS queries are generally restricted to standard record types like A, AAAA, and SRV. Embedding custom operational attributes in TXT records and parsing them for dynamic service discovery is highly inefficient and not natively supported by ECS service discovery.

options.text: Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Create an AWS Lambda function that triggers on ECS task state changes to update parameters with service IPs and custom attributes. Configure services to query Parameter Store for endpoint discovery.
options.explanation: Incorrect: This approach introduces significant custom development and operational overhead. Parameter Store is not designed for high-frequency, dynamic service discovery queries, and building a custom Lambda-based synchronizer is prone to race conditions and eventual consistency issues.

options.text: Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and configure advanced path-based routing for all microservices. Require services to discover each other by querying the ALB endpoint and passing custom HTTP headers to specify the required attributes.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Relying on an Application Load Balancer for service discovery by passing custom HTTP headers is not a standard or scalable service discovery pattern. It introduces a central point of failure and bottleneck for all internal microservice-to-microservice communication.

options.text: Use AWS Cloud Map with an HTTP namespace. Configure the Amazon ECS services to register with Cloud Map. Allow applications to discover services by querying the Cloud Map API using custom attributes, bypassing traditional DNS limitations.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Cloud Map is a cloud resource discovery service. By using an HTTP namespace, services register themselves via the API and can include custom attributes. Other services can then query the Cloud Map API to find endpoints matching specific custom attributes.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Cloud Map allows you to register any application resources, such as Amazon ECS tasks, Amazon EC2 instances, or Amazon DynamoDB tables, with custom names and attributes. When using an HTTP namespace, applications can use the Cloud Map DiscoverInstances API to filter and find endpoints based on those specific custom attributes, overcoming the limitations of standard DNS.

pt.domainName: Domínio 1: Design de Soluções para Complexidade Organizacional
pt.statement: Uma empresa de software opera centenas de microsserviços usando o Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Eles exigem um mecanismo dinâmico de descoberta de serviço que permita que os serviços se descubram. Crucialmente, alguns serviços devem descobrir endpoints consultando atributos operacionais personalizados em vez de depender apenas de endereços IP padrão e números de porta.

options.text: Usar zonas hospedadas privadas do Amazon Route 53 e configurar os serviços do Amazon ECS para registrar seus endereços IP como registros A. Usar consultas DNS padrão para descobrir serviços com base em atributos personalizados incorporados nos registros TXT.
options.explanation: Incorreto: As consultas DNS geralmente são restritas a tipos de registro padrão como A, AAAA e SRV. Incorporar atributos operacionais personalizados em registros TXT e analisá-los para descoberta dinâmica de serviços é altamente ineficiente e não tem suporte nativo para a descoberta de serviços do ECS.

options.text: Usar o AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Criar uma função AWS Lambda que é acionada por mudanças de estado de tarefa do ECS para atualizar parâmetros com IPs de serviço e atributos personalizados. Configurar serviços para consultar o Parameter Store para descoberta de endpoints.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Essa abordagem introduz desenvolvimento personalizado e sobrecarga operacional significativos. O Parameter Store não foi projetado para consultas dinâmicas de descoberta de serviço de alta frequência, e criar um sincronizador personalizado baseado em Lambda está sujeito a condições de corrida e problemas de consistência eventual.

options.text: Implantar um Application Load Balancer (ALB) e configurar o roteamento avançado baseado em caminho para todos os microsserviços. Exigir que os serviços se descubram consultando o endpoint do ALB e passando cabeçalhos HTTP personalizados para especificar os atributos necessários.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Depender de um Application Load Balancer para a descoberta de serviços passando cabeçalhos HTTP personalizados não é um padrão de descoberta de serviços padronizado ou escalável. Ele introduz um ponto central de falha e um gargalo para toda a comunicação interna entre microsserviços.

options.text: Usar o AWS Cloud Map com um namespace HTTP. Configurar os serviços do Amazon ECS para se registrarem no Cloud Map. Permitir que os aplicativos descubram serviços consultando a API do Cloud Map usando atributos personalizados, ignorando as limitações do DNS tradicional.
options.explanation: Correto: O AWS Cloud Map é um serviço de descoberta de recursos de nuvem. Ao usar um namespace HTTP, os serviços se registram via API e podem incluir atributos personalizados. Outros serviços podem então consultar a API do Cloud Map para encontrar endpoints que correspondam a atributos personalizados específicos.

pt.generalExplanation: O AWS Cloud Map permite que você registre quaisquer recursos de aplicativo, como tarefas do Amazon ECS, instâncias do Amazon EC2 ou tabelas do Amazon DynamoDB, com nomes e atributos personalizados. Ao usar um namespace HTTP, os aplicativos podem usar a API Cloud Map DiscoverInstances para filtrar e encontrar endpoints baseados nesses atributos personalizados específicos, superando as limitações do DNS padrão.

De manera crucial, algunos servicios deben descubrir endpoints consultando atributos operativos personalizados en lugar de depender únicamente de direcciones IP y números de puerto estándar.

options.text: Usar zonas alojadas privadas de Amazon Route 53 y configurar los servicios de Amazon ECS para registrar sus direcciones IP como registros A. Usar consultas DNS estándar para descubrir servicios según atributos personalizados integrados en los registros TXT.

options.text: Usar AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. options.explanation: Incorrecto: Este enfoque introduce un desarrollo personalizado y una sobrecarga operativa significativos. options.text: Implementar un Application Load Balancer (ALB) y configurar el enrutamiento avanzado basado en rutas para todos los microservicios. Requerir que los servicios se descubran entre sí consultando el endpoint de ALB y pasando encabezados HTTP personalizados para especificar los atributos requeridos.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: Depender de un Application Load Balancer para el descubrimiento de servicios mediante la transmisión de encabezados HTTP personalizados no es un patrón de descubrimiento de servicios estándar o escalable. Introduce un punto central de falla y un cuello de botella para toda la comunicación interna de microservicio a microservicio.

options.text: Usar AWS Cloud Map con un espacio de nombres HTTP. Configurar los servicios de Amazon ECS para registrarse en Cloud Map. Permitir que las aplicaciones descubran servicios consultando la API de Cloud Map mediante atributos personalizados, omitiendo las limitaciones de DNS tradicionales.
options.explanation: Correcto: AWS Cloud Map es un servicio de descubrimiento de recursos en la nube. Al usar un espacio de nombres HTTP, los servicios se registran a través de la API y pueden incluir atributos personalizados. Otros servicios pueden consultar la API de Cloud Map para encontrar endpoints que coincidan con atributos personalizados específicos.

es.generalExplanation: AWS Cloud Map le permite registrar cualquier recurso de aplicación, como tareas de Amazon ECS, instancias de Amazon EC2 o tablas de Amazon DynamoDB, con nombres y atributos personalizados. questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: A global enterprise has multiple business units operating independently across different AWS Regions and accounts. They need a networking architecture that provides global connectivity between regional hubs, while also allowing individual application teams to build and discover cross-account microservices without dealing with IP overlaps or complex routing configurations. Which combination of services should a Solutions Architect use to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use AWS Cloud WAN to establish a global core network, connecting regional VPCs and standardizing inter-region routing through centrally managed network segments and attachment policies.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Cloud WAN provides a managed wide area network that simplifies global connectivity. It allows you to build a centralized core network across multiple regions, handling routing and segmentation without the overhead of managing complex peering connections.

options.text: Use AWS Transit Gateway with inter-region peering to connect all regional VPCs, manually managing the route tables and handling overlapping IP address spaces using Private NAT Gateways.
options.explanation: Incorrect: While Transit Gateway with peering can provide global connectivity, it requires manual configuration of route tables and complex setups like Private NAT Gateways to handle IP overlaps, which significantly increases the operational overhead compared to Cloud WAN.

options.text: Use Amazon VPC Lattice to create a service network spanning multiple accounts and VPCs, enabling service discovery and secure connectivity for microservices regardless of the underlying IP addresses.
options.explanation: Correct: Amazon VPC Lattice abstracts away network complexity by providing a consistent way to discover, connect, and secure services across multiple VPCs and accounts, natively handling IP address overlaps and eliminating the need for complex routing configurations.

options.text: Deploy AWS App Mesh across all accounts to manage service-to-service communication, using a centralized AWS Cloud Map namespace for global service discovery and cross-region routing.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS App Mesh requires deploying and managing Envoy proxy sidecars for all workloads, which adds operational overhead. It also does not natively solve cross-account and cross-VPC networking complexities as seamlessly as VPC Lattice does.

options.text: Implement AWS PrivateLink by creating VPC Endpoint Services in each region and configuring VPC Peering across regions to allow cross-region endpoint access for microservices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Using AWS PrivateLink requires managing individual endpoint services and interface endpoints for every microservice. Combining this with cross-region VPC peering introduces massive complexity and scaling challenges, failing to meet the requirement for minimal operational overhead.

questions.generalExplanation: To provide a scalable architecture with minimal operational overhead, AWS Cloud WAN can be used to easily establish and manage the global core network and inter-region connectivity. Concurrently, Amazon VPC Lattice is ideal for the application layer, allowing microservices across different accounts and VPCs to connect and discover each other seamlessly, inherently resolving issues like overlapping IP spaces without complex routing tables.

pt.domainName: Domínio 1: Design de Soluções para Complexidade Organizacional
pt.statement: Uma empresa global tem várias unidades de negócios operando de forma independente em diferentes regiões e contas da AWS. Eles precisam de uma arquitetura de rede que forneça conectividade global entre hubs regionais, permitindo também que equipes de aplicativos individuais construam e descubram microsserviços entre contas sem lidar com sobreposições de IP ou configurações complexas de roteamento. Qual combinação de serviços um Arquiteto de Soluções deve usar para atender a esses requisitos com a MENOR sobrecarga operacional? (Selecione DUAS.)

options.text: Usar o AWS Cloud WAN para estabelecer uma rede central global, conectando VPCs regionais e padronizando o roteamento inter-regiões através de segmentos de rede e políticas de anexação gerenciados centralmente.
options.explanation: Correto: O AWS Cloud WAN fornece uma rede de longa distância gerenciada que simplifica a conectividade global. Ele permite que você crie uma rede centralizada em várias regiões, lidando com roteamento e segmentação sem a sobrecarga de gerenciar conexões complexas de peering.

options.text: Usar o AWS Transit Gateway com peering inter-regiões para conectar todas as VPCs regionais, gerenciando manualmente as tabelas de rotas e lidando com espaços de endereços IP sobrepostos usando NAT Gateways Privados.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Embora o Transit Gateway com peering possa fornecer conectividade global, ele requer a configuração manual de tabelas de rotas e configurações complexas como Private NAT Gateways para lidar com sobreposições de IP, o que aumenta significativamente a sobrecarga operacional em comparação com o Cloud WAN.

options.text: Usar o Amazon VPC Lattice para criar uma rede de serviços abrangendo várias contas e VPCs, permitindo a descoberta de serviços e conectividade segura para microsserviços, independentemente dos endereços IP subjacentes.
options.explanation: Correto: O Amazon VPC Lattice abstrai a complexidade da rede fornecendo uma maneira consistente de descobrir, conectar e proteger serviços em várias VPCs e contas, lidando nativamente com sobreposições de endereços IP e eliminando a necessidade de configurações de roteamento complexas.

options.text: Implantar o AWS App Mesh em todas as contas para gerenciar a comunicação entre serviços, usando um namespace centralizado do AWS Cloud Map para descoberta de serviços globais e roteamento entre regiões.
options.explanation: Incorreto: O AWS App Mesh exige a implantação e o gerenciamento de sidecars do proxy Envoy para todas as cargas de trabalho, o que aumenta a sobrecarga operacional. Ele também não resolve nativamente as complexidades de rede entre contas e entre VPCs tão perfeitamente quanto o VPC Lattice.

options.text: Implementar o AWS PrivateLink criando Serviços de Endpoint da VPC em cada região e configurando o Peering da VPC em várias regiões para permitir o acesso de endpoints entre regiões para microsserviços.
options.explanation: Incorreto: O uso do AWS PrivateLink exige o gerenciamento de serviços de endpoint e endpoints de interface individuais para cada microsserviço. Combinar isso com o peering de VPC entre regiões introduz enormes desafios de complexidade e escalabilidade, falhando em atender ao requisito de sobrecarga operacional mínima.

pt.generalExplanation: Para fornecer uma arquitetura escalável com sobrecarga operacional mínima, o AWS Cloud WAN pode ser usado para estabelecer e gerenciar facilmente a rede central global e a conectividade entre regiões. Ao mesmo tempo, o Amazon VPC Lattice é ideal para a camada de aplicativo, permitindo que microsserviços em diferentes contas e VPCs se conectem e descubram uns aos outros de forma perfeita, resolvendo de forma inerente problemas como sobreposição de espaços IP sem tabelas de roteamento complexas.

es.statement: Una empresa global tiene múltiples unidades de negocio que operan de forma independiente en diferentes regiones y cuentas de AWS. Necesitan una arquitectura de red que proporcione conectividad global entre centros regionales, al tiempo que permite a los equipos de aplicaciones individuales construir y descubrir microservicios entre cuentas sin lidiar con superposiciones de IP o configuraciones de enrutamiento complejas. ¿Qué combinación de servicios debería usar un Arquitecto de Soluciones para cumplir con estos requisitos con la MENOR sobrecarga operativa? (Seleccione DOS.)

options.text: Usar AWS Cloud WAN para establecer una red central global, conectando VPC regionales y estandarizando el enrutamiento interregional a través de segmentos de red y políticas de conexión administradas de forma centralizada.
options.explanation: Correcto: AWS Cloud WAN proporciona una red de área amplia administrada que simplifica la conectividad global. Le permite construir una red centralizada a través de múltiples regiones, manejando el enrutamiento y la segmentación sin la sobrecarga de administrar conexiones complejas de peering.

options.text: Usar AWS Transit Gateway con peering interregional para conectar todas las VPC regionales, administrando manualmente las tablas de rutas y manejando los espacios de direcciones IP superpuestas usando Private NAT Gateways.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: Aunque Transit Gateway con peering puede proporcionar conectividad global, requiere la configuración manual de tablas de rutas y configuraciones complejas como Private NAT Gateways para manejar las superposiciones de IP, lo que aumenta significativamente la sobrecarga operativa en comparación con Cloud WAN.

options.text: Usar Amazon VPC Lattice para crear una red de servicios que abarque varias cuentas y VPC, permitiendo el descubrimiento de servicios y la conectividad segura para microservicios, independientemente de las direcciones IP subyacentes.
options.explanation: Correcto: Amazon VPC Lattice abstrae la complejidad de la red al proporcionar una forma coherente de descubrir, conectar y asegurar servicios a través de múltiples VPC y cuentas, manejando de forma nativa las superposiciones de direcciones IP y eliminando la necesidad de configuraciones de enrutamiento complejas.

options.text: Implementar AWS App Mesh en todas las cuentas para administrar la comunicación de servicio a servicio, utilizando un espacio de nombres centralizado de AWS Cloud Map para el descubrimiento de servicios globales y el enrutamiento entre regiones.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: AWS App Mesh requiere implementar y administrar sidecars de proxy Envoy para todas las cargas de trabajo, lo que agrega sobrecarga operativa. Tampoco resuelve de forma nativa las complejidades de las redes entre cuentas y entre VPC tan perfectamente como lo hace VPC Lattice.

options.text: Implementar AWS PrivateLink mediante la creación de Servicios de Endpoint de VPC en cada región y la configuración de VPC Peering entre regiones para permitir el acceso de endpoints entre regiones para microservicios.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: El uso de AWS PrivateLink requiere administrar servicios de endpoint y endpoints de interfaz individuales para cada microservicio. questions.domainName: Domain 3: Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions
questions.statement: An enterprise uses AWS Organizations with dozens of accounts. Security policies dictate that no Amazon S3 buckets or IAM roles should grant access to external entities outside the Organization. The security team wants an automated way to continuously detect and be alerted when any resource policy or IAM role is misconfigured to allow external access.

options.text: Enable AWS IAM Access Analyzer at the organization level with the organization set as the zone of trust. Configure Amazon EventBridge rules to trigger alerts via Amazon SNS whenever Access Analyzer generates a finding for external access.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS IAM Access Analyzer uses automated reasoning to continuously analyze resource policies and IAM roles. By setting the organization as the zone of trust, it automatically generates findings for any policies granting access outside the organization, which can trigger EventBridge.

options.text: Use AWS Config rules (`s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited` and `iam-role-managed-policy-check`) across all accounts. Use an AWS Systems Manager Automation document to automatically remediate non-compliant resources and send email alerts.
options.explanation: Incorrect: These specific AWS Config rules check for public S3 buckets and specific managed policies, but they do not dynamically analyze complex IAM trust policies and S3 resource policies for cross-account sharing with specific external principals outside the AWS Organization.

options.text: Enable Amazon Macie across the organization and configure it to scan all S3 buckets for public access. Deploy a custom AWS Lambda function to periodically scan all IAM roles for external trust relationships.
options.explanation: Incorrect: While Amazon Macie can detect public S3 buckets, it is primarily designed for data classification and discovery, not for comprehensive IAM role trust policy analysis. Using a custom Lambda function for IAM scanning is inefficient and prone to errors.

options.text: Configure AWS CloudTrail to log all `PutBucketPolicy` and `UpdateAssumeRolePolicy` API calls. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs metric filters to detect external principal ARNs and trigger a CloudWatch Alarm.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Relying solely on CloudTrail and regex metric filters is brittle and highly inaccurate. It cannot holistically evaluate the mathematical logic of complex IAM policies to determine if access is actually granted to an external entity, unlike the formal logic used by Access Analyzer.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS IAM Access Analyzer helps you identify the resources in your organization and accounts, such as Amazon S3 buckets or IAM roles, that are shared with an external entity. By defining the AWS Organization as the zone of trust, Access Analyzer continuously monitors policies and alerts you via EventBridge if any resource allows access from outside your organizational boundaries.

questions.domainName: Domain 3: Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions
questions.statement: A large company is building a centralized network architecture using AWS Transit Gateway and Amazon Route 53 Resolver in a shared networking account. They need to securely share the Transit Gateway and Route 53 Resolver rules with 100+ application accounts managed under AWS Organizations, ensuring that only accounts within specific Organizational Units (OUs) have access.

options.text: Create a cross-account IAM Role in the networking account that allows `sts:AssumeRole` for all application accounts. Modify the Transit Gateway and Route 53 Resolver resource policies to allow the assumed roles to connect.
options.explanation: Incorrect: You cannot share Transit Gateway attachments or Route 53 Resolver rules simply by assuming cross-account IAM roles or modifying resource policies. These are account-level resources that must be natively shared across accounts.

options.text: Establish VPC Peering connections between the shared networking account and all 100+ application accounts. Manually configure the route tables and DNS settings in each application account to point to the shared networking resources.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Using VPC Peering for 100+ accounts defeats the purpose of using a centralized Transit Gateway, introducing massive operational overhead, route table complexity, and lacking a mechanism to seamlessly share Route 53 Resolver rules.

options.text: Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) in the networking account. Create a resource share containing the Transit Gateway and Route 53 Resolver rules, and specify the target Organizational Units (OUs) as principals for the share.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) is the natively supported service to securely share resources like Transit Gateways, Route 53 Resolver rules, and Subnets. By targeting specific OUs in AWS Organizations, it automates access management efficiently.

options.text: Use AWS Service Catalog to create products for the Transit Gateway attachments and Route 53 Resolver rules. Share the Service Catalog portfolio with the organization so application teams can provision the resources themselves.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Service Catalog is used for standardizing infrastructure provisioning, not for sharing existing centralized network instances (like a Transit Gateway or Resolver Rules) across accounts. It would result in deploying duplicate resources instead of sharing them.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) helps you securely share your resources across AWS accounts, within your organization or organizational units (OUs), and with IAM roles and users. It is the architectural standard for sharing centralized networking infrastructure such as AWS Transit Gateway, AWS Cloud WAN core networks, and Amazon Route 53 Resolver rules.

questions.statement: A healthcare organization stores large volumes of patient data in Amazon S3 buckets across multiple AWS accounts. To meet compliance requirements, the security team needs a solution to automatically discover and classify Protected Health Information (PHI) and Personally Identifiable Information (PII) stored in these buckets, providing a centralized dashboard of data security posture.

options.text: Enable Amazon Macie in a delegated administrator account for the AWS Organization. Configure automated sensitive data discovery jobs to scan S3 buckets across all accounts for PHI and PII, centralizing the findings in the administrator account.
options.explanation: Correct: Amazon Macie is a data security and data privacy service that uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover and protect sensitive data (like PII and PHI) in AWS. It integrates with AWS Organizations for centralized administration and visibility.

options.text: Deploy AWS DataSync to copy all S3 bucket data to a centralized account. Use AWS Glue crawlers to catalog the data and Amazon Athena to query for PHI and PII patterns using complex SQL regular expressions.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Copying all data via DataSync to a single account is inefficient, expensive, and introduces significant security risks. Using Glue and Athena to parse text for PHI/PII via regex is incredibly resource-intensive and prone to high false-positive rates compared to Macie.

options.text: Configure Amazon S3 Object Lambda for all buckets to inspect `GetObject` requests in real-time. If the requested object contains PHI or PII, trigger an Amazon EventBridge event to notify the security team via Amazon SNS.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 Object Lambda modifies data as it is being retrieved by an application. It is not designed to perform asynchronous, full-bucket discovery and classification of data at rest, and checking every `GetObject` request for complex PII patterns would severely degrade performance.

options.text: Enable AWS Security Hub across all accounts. Use the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard to automatically detect PII in S3 buckets and aggregate the compliance scores in a central dashboard.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Security Hub provides a comprehensive view of security alerts and security posture, but it does not natively scan the *content* of S3 objects for sensitive data like PHI or PII. It relies on Amazon Macie for that specific capability.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon Macie is a fully managed data security and data privacy service that uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover and protect your sensitive data in AWS. It natively understands complex data types like PHI and PII, scales automatically across millions of S3 objects, and integrates with AWS Organizations for central management.

questions.domainName: Domain 3: Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions
questions.statement: An e-commerce company hosts its web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and Amazon CloudFront. During peak shopping seasons, they frequently experience sophisticated Layer 7 DDoS attacks and massive volumetric attacks. They need a comprehensive protection strategy that automatically mitigates these attacks, provides near real-time visibility, and offers financial protection against scaling costs. Which combination of actions should the Solutions Architect take? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced and add the CloudFront distribution and the Application Load Balancer as protected resources to enable automated application layer DDoS mitigation.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Shield Advanced provides expanded DDoS attack protection for web applications running on resources like CloudFront and ALBs. It offers near real-time visibility into attacks, integration with WAF, and DDoS cost protection to safeguard against scaling charges.

options.text: Deploy AWS Network Firewall in front of the Application Load Balancer to inspect all incoming HTTP/HTTPS traffic and automatically drop packets associated with volumetric DDoS attacks.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Network Firewall operates within the VPC and cannot effectively absorb massive volumetric DDoS attacks before they enter the AWS network. CloudFront and Shield Advanced are the proper edge-layer defenses for volumetric attacks.

options.text: Configure AWS WAF web ACLs and associate them with the protected CloudFront distribution and ALB. Enable rate-based rules and AWS Shield Advanced automatic application layer DDoS mitigation.
options.explanation: Correct: Integrating AWS WAF with Shield Advanced allows Shield to automatically create, test, and deploy WAF rules to mitigate sophisticated Layer 7 DDoS attacks, fulfilling the requirement for automated application layer protection.

options.text: Enable Amazon GuardDuty and configure it to automatically block malicious IP addresses at the CloudFront level by updating the distribution's geographic restriction settings in real-time.
options.explanation: Incorrect: GuardDuty does not have a native, built-in feature to automatically update CloudFront geographic restrictions in real-time. This would require custom Lambda automation, which adds operational overhead and is less effective than WAF/Shield.

options.text: Subscribe to AWS Shield Standard and submit a limit increase request to the AWS Support Center to enable financial protection and proactive engagement from the AWS DDoS Response Team (DRT).
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Shield Standard provides basic protection but does NOT include financial protection against scaling costs, nor does it include proactive engagement from the AWS Shield Response Team (SRT/DRT). These features are exclusive to Shield Advanced.

questions.generalExplanation: To achieve comprehensive protection against sophisticated Layer 7 and massive volumetric DDoS attacks, you must use AWS Shield Advanced and AWS WAF together at the edge (CloudFront). Shield Advanced provides volumetric protection, real-time visibility, and cost protection. Integrating it with WAF enables automatic application layer (Layer 7) DDoS mitigation, where Shield analyzes traffic baselines and automatically creates WAF rules to block anomalies.

Their data center has a dedicated 1 Gbps internet connection, but it is heavily utilized by production workloads. The migration must be completed securely within two months.

options.text: Order an AWS Snowmobile to be dispatched to the on-premises data center. Transfer the data locally to the Snowmobile via high-speed network connections. Once the data is imported into an Amazon S3 Standard bucket, use S3 Lifecycle policies to transition the data to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Snowmobile is an exabyte-scale data transfer service capable of moving up to 100 PB per vehicle. It is the only feasible option to move 50 PB within two months. Data is first imported to S3 Standard, and then Lifecycle policies must be used to move it to Glacier.

options.text: Order multiple AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices. Transfer the data locally and ship them back to AWS. Import the data directly into Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive, then transition to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval to save costs.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Migrating 50 PB using Snowball Edge devices (around 80 TB usable each) would require over 600 devices, making it logistically complex and practically impossible to complete within two months. Furthermore, you cannot import data directly into S3 Glacier Deep Archive via Snowball.

options.text: Provision an AWS Direct Connect connection with a 10 Gbps dedicated link. Use AWS DataSync to migrate the 50 PB of data directly to an Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval bucket over the network.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Provisioning a new dedicated Direct Connect link takes significant time. Even with a dedicated 10 Gbps connection constantly fully saturated, transferring 50 PB of data would take well over a year, failing to meet the strict two-month deadline.

options.text: Use AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway to create cached volumes backed by Amazon S3. Expose the volumes to the on-premises servers via iSCSI and gradually write the 50 PB of data, allowing the gateway to upload the data asynchronously.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Storage Gateway uses the existing internet connection to upload data. Transferring 50 PB of data over a partially utilized 1 Gbps internet connection would literally take decades to complete, making this approach entirely unfeasible for the given timeline.

questions.generalExplanation: For migrations of massive datasets in the multi-petabyte to exabyte range under strict time constraints, physical data transfer using AWS Snowmobile is the mathematically and logistically sound approach. questions.domainName: Domain 4: Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization
questions.statement: A research institute processes genomic data using thousands of parallel batch jobs. The workloads are containerized, highly resilient to interruptions, and have variable execution times ranging from 10 minutes to 3 hours. The institute wants to minimize compute costs and orchestrate these jobs dynamically without provisioning or managing underlying instances.

options.text: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with managed node groups backed by Spot Instances. Deploy a custom Kubernetes controller to schedule the batch jobs and scale the cluster based on the custom metrics from Amazon CloudWatch.
options.explanation: Incorrect: While EKS supports Spot Instances, deploying and managing custom Kubernetes controllers for batch scheduling and scaling based on CloudWatch metrics introduces significant operational overhead compared to a fully managed batch service.

options.text: Create an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group with Spot Instances. Use Amazon SQS to queue the jobs and deploy a custom worker script on the EC2 instances to pull messages, run the Docker containers, and terminate instances when the queue is empty.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Building a custom orchestration system using Auto Scaling groups, SQS, and custom worker scripts requires substantial ongoing maintenance and development effort, failing the requirement to dynamically orchestrate jobs without managing the underlying instances and scaling logic.

options.text: Deploy the containerized jobs to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) using the AWS Fargate launch type. Configure an AWS Step Functions state machine to orchestrate the parallel execution of the thousands of containers.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Fargate is typically more expensive than EC2 Spot Instances. Additionally, using AWS Step Functions to orchestrate thousands of parallel containers running for up to 3 hours could hit state machine limits and become complex to manage compared to AWS Batch queues.

options.text: Use AWS Batch configured with a Managed Compute Environment utilizing Spot Instances. Use the `BEST_FIT_PROGRESSIVE` allocation strategy and configure the job queues to automatically scale and schedule the containerized jobs based on priority.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Batch is fully managed and designed specifically for orchestrating parallel batch workloads. By using a Managed Compute Environment with Spot Instances and the `BEST_FIT_PROGRESSIVE` strategy, it automatically optimizes scheduling, instance selection, and scaling at the lowest possible cost.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Batch provides a fully managed environment designed specifically for running hundreds of thousands of batch computing jobs. For interruption-tolerant workloads, configuring an AWS Batch Managed Compute Environment to use EC2 Spot Instances drastically minimizes compute costs. AWS Batch handles the underlying infrastructure provisioning, scaling, and job scheduling natively, eliminating operational overhead.

questions.domainName: Domain 4: Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization
questions.statement: A company recently migrated hundreds of applications to Amazon EC2 and Amazon EBS. The finance team noticed higher than expected costs and requested the engineering team to right-size the infrastructure. They need a centralized, automated way to identify over-provisioned EC2 instances and underutilized EBS volumes across all AWS accounts, along with specific resizing recommendations.

options.text: Enable Amazon CloudWatch Detailed Monitoring for all EC2 instances. Use AWS Lambda functions to analyze CPU, Memory, and Disk IOPS metrics, and generate an Amazon SNS notification when utilization falls below 20% for a consecutive 7-day period.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Writing custom Lambda functions to analyze metrics for hundreds of instances across multiple accounts introduces significant development and operational overhead. It also lacks the machine-learning-driven recommendations for specific target instance types.

options.text: Enable AWS Compute Optimizer at the organization level. Ensure the AWS Systems Manager Agent is installed and configured to collect memory metrics. Use the Compute Optimizer dashboard to view machine-learning-based right-sizing recommendations for EC2 instances and EBS volumes.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Compute Optimizer uses machine learning to analyze historical resource utilization. By enabling it at the organization level and supplying memory metrics via SSM, it provides precise, automated right-sizing recommendations for both EC2 and EBS to reduce costs.

options.text: Use AWS Trusted Advisor to review the cost optimization checks. Rely on the 'Low Utilization Amazon EC2 Instances' check to automatically modify the instance types and EBS volume types to the recommended lower-cost alternatives using AWS Systems Manager Automation.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Trusted Advisor can identify low utilization resources, but it does not automatically execute changes, nor does it provide the advanced machine-learning-based specific instance family and size recommendations that Compute Optimizer offers.

options.text: Configure AWS Cost and Usage Reports (CUR) to deliver daily reports to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the reports for resources with low utilization metrics and build an Amazon QuickSight dashboard to visualize the over-provisioned resources.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Cost and Usage Reports (CUR) detail billing information but do not contain granular, time-series performance metrics (like CPU or memory utilization percentages) required to mathematically determine if an instance is over-provisioned or to recommend a specific replacement.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Compute Optimizer is the native AWS service designed to deliver right-sizing recommendations for compute resources, including EC2 instances, EBS volumes, and Lambda functions. It uses machine learning to analyze historical performance metrics and provides specific recommendations for instance types to optimize costs without sacrificing performance. It also integrates with AWS Organizations for multi-account visibility.

questions.domainName: Domain 4: Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization
questions.statement: A SaaS company runs a complex microservices architecture on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). They want to implement advanced traffic routing strategies, such as canary deployments and A/B testing, without modifying the application code. They also need end-to-end mutual TLS (mTLS) encryption between the microservices for compliance.

options.text: Configure the AWS Load Balancer Controller to provision an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Use the ALB's advanced routing rules to split traffic between different Kubernetes services for canary deployments. Terminate TLS at the ALB and use unencrypted traffic internally.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Terminating TLS at the ALB leaves internal pod-to-pod communication unencrypted, which fails the explicit requirement for end-to-end mutual TLS (mTLS) encryption between the microservices for compliance purposes.

options.text: Implement AWS App Mesh and deploy the Envoy proxy as a sidecar to the microservices pods in the EKS cluster. Use App Mesh Virtual Routers and Routes to manage traffic splitting for canary deployments, and enable mTLS within the App Mesh configuration for end-to-end encryption.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS App Mesh is a service mesh that uses Envoy proxy sidecars. It abstracts networking logic from the application code, natively supporting advanced routing like canary deployments and seamlessly implementing mutual TLS (mTLS) between microservices.

options.text: Deploy Amazon API Gateway in front of the EKS cluster. Configure API Gateway to handle the canary deployments by splitting traffic between multiple integration endpoints. Enforce mTLS using AWS WAF and AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) on the API Gateway.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Amazon API Gateway handles ingress traffic from clients but is not designed to manage internal service-to-service (east-west) traffic routing and mTLS encryption between pods within an EKS cluster.

options.text: Use AWS Cloud Map for service discovery within the EKS cluster. Modify the application code of each microservice to query Cloud Map for the available endpoints and implement client-side load balancing and mTLS certificate verification.
options.explanation: Incorrect: The scenario explicitly requires achieving these networking and security goals *without modifying the application code*. Forcing microservices to perform custom client-side load balancing and certificate validation violates this constraint.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS App Mesh is a service mesh that standardizes how your microservices communicate, giving you end-to-end visibility and helping to ensure high availability for your applications. By deploying Envoy proxies as sidecars, App Mesh handles all intra-cluster routing (enabling canary and A/B deployments) and security (enabling mTLS) transparently, requiring zero changes to the actual application code.

options.text: Configurar o AWS Load Balancer Controller para provisionar um Application Load Balancer (ALB). options.text: Implementar o AWS App Mesh e implantar o proxy Envoy como um sidecar nos pods de microsserviços no cluster EKS. Usar Virtual Routers e Routes do App Mesh para gerenciar a divisão de tráfego para implantações canárias e habilitar o mTLS na configuração do App Mesh para criptografia de ponta a ponta.
options.explanation: Correto: O AWS App Mesh é uma malha de serviço que usa sidecars do proxy Envoy. Ele abstrai a lógica de rede do código do aplicativo, suportando nativamente roteamento avançado como implantações de canário e implementando perfeitamente TLS mútuo (mTLS) entre microsserviços.

options.text: Usar o AWS Cloud Map para descoberta de serviços dentro do cluster EKS. Modificar o código do aplicativo de cada microsserviço para consultar o Cloud Map para os endpoints disponíveis e implementar o balanceamento de carga do lado do cliente e a verificação do certificado mTLS.

questions.domainName: Domain 4: Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization
questions.statement: A company is modernizing a monolithic application by breaking it down into containerized microservices. They plan to deploy these microservices on Amazon EKS using AWS Fargate to remove the operational burden of managing EC2 nodes. They need to ensure that the Fargate pods are right-sized over time to avoid over-provisioning compute resources, and they require strict network isolation between different microservices within the cluster. Which combination of actions should the Solutions Architect take? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Enable AWS Compute Optimizer for the AWS account. Use Compute Optimizer to analyze the CPU and memory utilization of the Amazon EKS workloads on AWS Fargate and apply the recommended pod sizing configurations.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Compute Optimizer supports EKS workloads on Fargate. It continuously analyzes CPU and memory metrics to provide right-sizing recommendations, helping avoid over-provisioning and ensuring cost efficiency.

options.text: Use AWS Cost Explorer Rightsizing Recommendations to analyze the historical resource utilization of the EKS cluster and automatically apply the recommended pod sizing adjustments via an AWS Lambda function.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Cost Explorer's Rightsizing Recommendations feature primarily focuses on Amazon EC2 instances and does not provide pod-level granularity or recommendations for AWS Fargate workloads running on Amazon EKS.

options.text: Implement Kubernetes Network Policies within the EKS cluster. Define rules to explicitly control the ingress and egress traffic between the different microservice pods running on AWS Fargate.
options.explanation: Correct: Kubernetes Network Policies are the standard and native way to enforce network isolation at the pod level within an EKS cluster. They allow granular control over which pods can communicate with each other, fulfilling the strict isolation requirement.

options.text: Configure AWS WAF web ACLs and associate them with the EKS cluster's VPC. Create custom rules to inspect and block unauthorized internal traffic between the microservice pods based on their IP addresses.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS WAF is a web application firewall designed for protecting edge resources (like ALBs, API Gateway, CloudFront) from external HTTP/HTTPS exploits. It is not designed to inspect and control internal pod-to-pod network traffic.

options.text: Create separate Amazon VPCs for each microservice. Deploy a Transit Gateway to connect the VPCs and use Security Groups to enforce strict network isolation between the services.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Deploying each microservice in its own separate VPC simply to achieve isolation is an extreme anti-pattern for Amazon EKS. It creates unnecessary complexity and completely defeats the purpose of running a centralized Kubernetes cluster.

questions.generalExplanation: When deploying modern microservices on Amazon EKS with AWS Fargate, AWS Compute Optimizer provides machine-learning-backed insights to correctly size CPU and memory configurations for pods, thereby optimizing costs. Simultaneously, to secure communication between these microservices, native Kubernetes Network Policies should be employed to restrict pod-to-pod (east-west) traffic within the cluster without resorting to complex infrastructure separation.

options.explanation: Incorreto: O AWS WAF é um firewall de aplicativo web projetado para proteger recursos de borda (como ALBs, API Gateway, CloudFront) contra exploits HTTP/HTTPS externos. Ele não foi projetado para inspecionar e controlar o tráfego de rede interno de pod a pod.

options.text: Criar VPCs da Amazon separadas para cada microsserviço. Implantar um Transit Gateway para conectar as VPCs e usar Security Groups para impor um isolamento rígido da rede entre os serviços.

pt.generalExplanation: Ao implantar microsserviços modernos no Amazon EKS com o AWS Fargate, o AWS Compute Optimizer fornece insights apoiados por aprendizado de máquina para dimensionar corretamente as configurações de CPU e memória para pods, otimizando os custos. options.text: Habilitar AWS Compute Optimizer para la cuenta de AWS. Usar Compute Optimizer para analizar el uso de CPU y memoria de las cargas de trabajo de Amazon EKS en AWS Fargate y aplicar las configuraciones de dimensionamiento de pods recomendadas.

options.text: Usar las Recomendaciones de Ajuste de Tamaño de AWS Cost Explorer para analizar el uso histórico de recursos del clúster de EKS y aplicar automáticamente los ajustes de tamaño de los pods recomendados a través de una función de AWS Lambda.

options.text: Crear VPC de Amazon separadas para cada microservicio. Implementar un Transit Gateway para conectar las VPC y usar Grupos de Seguridad para aplicar un estricto aislamiento de red entre los servicios.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: A social media platform is experiencing significant performance issues when querying their relational database to find complex relationships, such as 'friends of friends who have liked the same posts.' The database queries require multiple recursive JOINs and are timing out. The company wants to migrate to a purpose-built database service to resolve these performance bottlenecks with the least amount of management overhead.

options.text: Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora Serverless v2. Use Aurora's auto-scaling capabilities to handle the high CPU load generated by the recursive JOIN queries during peak usage.
options.explanation: Incorrect: While Aurora Serverless v2 scales compute rapidly, relational databases are fundamentally not optimized for highly connected relationship queries. Complex recursive JOINs will still perform poorly and consume massive resources regardless of auto-scaling.

options.text: Migrate the relationship data to Amazon Neptune. Re-model the data as a graph and use query languages like Gremlin or openCypher to traverse the highly connected dataset efficiently without complex JOINs.
options.explanation: Correct: Amazon Neptune is a fully managed, purpose-built graph database designed to store billions of relationships and query them with millisecond latency. It completely eliminates the need for expensive recursive JOINs found in relational databases.

options.text: Use Amazon DynamoDB to store the relationship data. Implement an AWS Lambda function to query DynamoDB multiple times recursively, maintaining the relationship logic in the application code.
options.explanation: Incorrect: DynamoDB is a key-value/document store, not a graph database. Forcing the application layer (Lambda) to execute multiple recursive queries to traverse relationships is highly inefficient, complex to maintain, and will result in high latency and costs.

options.text: Migrate the data to Amazon Redshift. Pre-calculate the relationships using complex SQL queries and store the results in materialized views to speed up read access for the application.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Amazon Redshift is an analytical data warehouse (OLAP), not a transactional database for social media platforms. Using it to pre-calculate friends-of-friends relationships via materialized views introduces high latency for real-time updates.

questions.generalExplanation: When dealing with highly connected datasets where the relationships between data points are just as important as the data itself (like social networks, fraud detection, or recommendation engines), relational databases suffer from performance degradation due to complex JOINs. Amazon Neptune is a purpose-built graph database optimized exactly for traversing these relationships in milliseconds.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: An industrial IoT company collects sensor data from millions of devices globally, inserting over 10 million data points per second. They need a database to store this time-series data, run analytics to identify trends over time, and automatically tier older data to lower-cost storage without managing servers or complex data lifecycle pipelines.

options.text: Use Amazon Timestream to ingest and store the sensor data. Configure Timestream's memory store for recent data and its magnetic store for historical data to automatically tier data based on retention policies, using its built-in time-series analytics functions.
options.explanation: Correct: Amazon Timestream is a fast, scalable, and serverless time-series database. It is purpose-built for IoT and operational applications, natively supporting built-in analytics functions and automatic data lifecycle tiering from a fast memory store to a cost-effective magnetic store.

options.text: Ingest the data into Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and use AWS Lambda to write the data to Amazon DynamoDB. Configure DynamoDB Time to Live (TTL) to automatically delete older data to reduce storage costs.
options.explanation: Incorrect: DynamoDB TTL deletes data instead of tiering it to a lower-cost storage for historical analysis. While DynamoDB can handle high ingestion rates, it lacks native time-series analytic functions (like interpolation or smoothing) found in Amazon Timestream.

options.text: Use Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with the TimescaleDB extension. Deploy it on a large EC2 instance class and manually partition the tables based on timestamps to improve query performance for time-series analytics.
options.explanation: Incorrect: The scenario specifically requests a solution without managing servers or complex data lifecycle pipelines. Deploying and managing RDS on a large instance class and manually partitioning tables introduces significant operational overhead and is not serverless.

options.text: Ingest data via Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose and deliver it to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the time-series data directly from S3, relying on S3 Lifecycle policies to transition data to Glacier.
options.explanation: Incorrect: While Athena can query data on S3, this architecture does not provide the sub-millisecond ingestion and real-time querying capabilities of an active memory store. Athena queries would be too slow for real-time operational dashboarding compared to Timestream.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon Timestream is an explicitly purpose-built serverless time-series database. It automatically scales to ingest trillions of events daily and manages the data lifecycle by tiering recent data in memory (for fast analytics) and older data to a magnetic store (for cost reduction), eliminating the need for custom lifecycle scripts or database tuning.

options.text: Usar o Amazon Timestream para ingerir e armazenar os dados do sensor. Implantar e gerenciar o RDS em uma classe de instância grande e particionar tabelas manualmente introduz uma sobrecarga operacional significativa e não é serverless.

questions.statement: An enterprise is migrating a legacy on-premises application to AWS. They need a fully managed AWS storage service that supports these native NetApp features and provides multi-AZ high availability to minimize changes to their existing operational workflows.

options.text: Use Amazon EFS with multi-AZ deployment. Reconfigure the application's disaster recovery workflows to use AWS Backup instead of SnapMirror, and use AWS Lambda to script snapshot cloning for testing.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Amazon EFS is an NFS file system but it does not support native NetApp ONTAP features. Forcing the enterprise to abandon SnapMirror and FlexClone in favor of custom scripts and AWS Backup violates the requirement to minimize changes to operational workflows.

options.text: Use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. Deploy it in a Multi-AZ configuration and use Microsoft Distributed File System Replication (DFS-R) to replicate data, rewriting the application's cloning logic.
options.explanation: Incorrect: FSx for Windows File Server provides SMB storage tailored for Windows environments, not NetApp ONTAP. It does not support SnapMirror or FlexClone, and attempting to rewrite the logic using DFS-R fails the objective.

options.text: Migrate the storage to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP in a Multi-AZ deployment. The service natively supports ONTAP features like SnapMirror and FlexClone, allowing the enterprise to retain their existing operational workflows and tooling.
options.explanation: Correct: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP provides fully managed shared storage built on NetApp's popular ONTAP file system. It natively supports SnapMirror, FlexClone, and SnapVault, allowing enterprises to migrate applications to AWS without altering their existing storage workflows.

options.text: Deploy NetApp Cloud Volumes ONTAP on Amazon EC2 instances. Configure an Auto Scaling group and use Amazon EBS volumes for storage, manually managing the high availability across Availability Zones.
options.explanation: Incorrect: While deploying Cloud Volumes ONTAP on EC2 provides ONTAP features, it is a self-managed solution, not a 'fully managed AWS storage service' as requested. The customer would be responsible for managing EC2 instances, EBS volumes, and high availability.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP provides fully managed shared storage that brings the popular data access and data management capabilities of ONTAP to AWS. questions.statement: A financial research firm is building a new application on AWS. They need a highly connected fraud-detection database that can perform sub-millisecond traverses across billions of relationships to detect money laundering rings. Additionally, they need an ultra-fast shared file storage solution for their Linux-based machine learning compute farm, which requires microsecond latencies and supports ZFS-based snapshots for rapid data experimentation. Which combination of services should the Solutions Architect use? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use Amazon Neptune for the fraud-detection database to efficiently store and traverse the billions of highly connected relationships using graph query languages.
options.explanation: Correct: Amazon Neptune is a fully managed graph database designed to process highly connected datasets (like fraud rings) with sub-millisecond latency, natively supporting graph traversals that would be extremely slow in relational databases.

options.text: Use Amazon DynamoDB for the fraud-detection database, designing a complex adjacency list pattern to traverse the billions of relationships using secondary indexes.
options.explanation: Incorrect: While DynamoDB is fast for key-value lookups, building a complex adjacency list to traverse billions of relationships for fraud detection introduces massive application-side complexity and cannot guarantee sub-millisecond recursive traversals like Neptune.

options.text: Use Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with the `pg_trgm` extension to build a relational schema capable of querying the billions of relationships using recursive SQL queries.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Recursive SQL queries (CTEs) on billions of rows in a relational database will perform poorly and will not meet the sub-millisecond latency requirement for deep graph traversals required in fraud detection.

options.text: Use Amazon FSx for OpenZFS to provide the Linux compute farm with ultra-fast shared file storage, leveraging its microsecond latencies and native ZFS snapshot capabilities.
options.explanation: Correct: Amazon FSx for OpenZFS provides fully managed shared file storage built on the OpenZFS file system. It delivers microsecond latencies for Linux workloads and natively supports ZFS-based snapshots and cloning for rapid data experimentation.

options.text: Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with Provisioned Throughput to provide the Linux compute farm with shared storage, using AWS Backup to create snapshots for data experimentation.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Amazon EFS provides millisecond latencies, not the microsecond latencies requested. Furthermore, it does not support native, instantaneous ZFS-based snapshots or cloning required for rapid machine learning data experimentation.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon Neptune is purpose-built for querying highly connected datasets such as fraud detection networks, easily performing sub-millisecond traversals over billions of relationships. For the machine learning compute farm requiring extreme performance, Amazon FSx for OpenZFS provides shared file storage with microsecond latencies, high throughput, and native OpenZFS features like instant snapshots and cloning.

options.text: Usar o Amazon Neptune para o banco de dados de detecção de fraude para armazenar e cruzar eficientemente bilhões de relacionamentos altamente conectados usando linguagens de consulta de grafos.
options.explanation: Correto: O Amazon Neptune é um banco de dados de grafos totalmente gerenciado, projetado para processar conjuntos de dados altamente conectados (como redes de fraude) com latência abaixo de um milissegundo, suportando nativamente cruzamentos de grafos que seriam extremamente lentos em bancos de dados relacionais.

options.text: Usar o Amazon DynamoDB para o banco de dados de detecção de fraude, projetando um padrão complexo de lista de adjacências para cruzar bilhões de relacionamentos usando índices secundários.
